standard.title: Evaluate idea organisation and its impact
standard.description: analyse the organisation of ideas in paragraphs and extended texts, and evaluate its impact on meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students explain how ideas are structured using taxonomies, cause and effect, metaphors and chronology (AC9E7LY04). They have not yet evaluated the impact of organisational choices on meaning — moving from describing organisation to assessing its effectiveness.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse the organisation of ideas in paragraphs and extended texts and evaluate its impact on meaning.

nodes.label: Techniques for organising ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify organisational techniques used in texts and explain what each technique does to the reader's experience of the ideas.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two organisational techniques in a text (e.g. juxtaposition, chronological reversal, exaggeration) and explain what each does to the arrangement of ideas.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse the techniques used in extended texts to organise ideas — examining comparison, contrast, exaggeration, juxtaposition, chronological manipulation, and expansion/compression of time.
wider: Compare how two texts covering the same event use different organisational techniques and assess which arrangement is more effective for their respective purposes
Examine how a text's organisation creates emotional effects — analysing how the sequence of information is designed to evoke particular responses

response_modes.reason: Students need a repertoire of organisational technique names and functions to analyse organisation at the level of choice rather than just sequence. Building this repertoire across diverse text types enables the evaluative work at node 2.

success_criteria: Student names an organisational technique and explains its function (not just describes the content sequence)
Student identifies how the technique shapes what the reader experiences — not just what information is present
nodes.hinge_reason: Evaluating impact at N2 requires named technique types — students without a repertoire of organisation techniques evaluate by intuition rather than evidence, which means the N2 evaluative judgement cannot be substantiated.

nodes.label: Evaluating impact on meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate the impact of organisational choices on meaning — making judgements about whether the arrangement conveys meaning effectively and supporting those judgements.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate the impact of one organisational choice in a text — making a supported judgement about whether it effectively conveys meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate techniques used in texts to organise ideas and evoke emotional responses — explaining whether the author conveys meaning effectively through the sequence of information and evidence, and making supported judgements.
wider: Reorder a section of a text and evaluate how the reorganisation changes the meaning or emotional impact — using the exercise to illuminate the effect of the original choices
Evaluate the organisational coherence of a student text and provide targeted feedback on one structural improvement

response_modes.reason: Evaluating organisational impact requires criteria — students need scaffolding for what makes an arrangement effective (does it serve the purpose? does it lead the reader through the argument? does it create the intended effect?). Without criteria, evaluation is preference rather than analysis.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Text organisation evaluation is directly connected to students' own writing development. The move from analysing to evaluating is a significant capability advance, and the connection to their own organisational choices makes this pedagogically productive territory.
success_criteria: Student makes a specific evaluative claim about an organisational choice (not just describes it)
Student supports the evaluation with reference to the text's purpose and the effect on meaning or reader response
